ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: I looked at the attached figure; point A is on the left, and point B is at the lower right. After the river flows rightward from A, it first splits into upper and lower branches; in the figure, the upper branch is labeled 2/3, and the lower branch continues along the bottom direction toward the lower right to B. After that, the upper 2/3 branch splits again into three branches: in the figure, one branch labeled 1/8 flows away toward the upper right, one branch labeled 5/8 flows away toward the right, and there is also one unlabeled branch that bends downward and joins the lower river channel leading to B. Reasoning: At the first split, the upper branch carries away 2/3 of the original water amount, so the lower branch directly leading to B carries away the remaining 1 - 2/3 = 1/3. Later the upper 2/3 branch splits into three branches, of which 1/8 and 5/8 do not flow to B; the one that flows to B is the remaining branch, which accounts for 1 - 1/8 - 5/8 = 2/8 = 1/4 of that upper branch. So this tributary joining B contributes (2/3)(1/4) = 1/6 of the original water amount. The total amount of water flowing to B is the lower original branch's 1/3 plus the later joined 1/6, namely 1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2.
